title: Relay header sets
description: The two header sets the connector controls on a relayed request: what it sends UPSTREAM to the loopback daemon (derived from lib/portal/proxy.js forwardHeaders and FORWARD, and lib/portal/ws-relay.js for the upgrade, both moving to lib/relay, C-06.4), and what it ADDS or REPLACES on the response it relays DOWNSTREAM to the hub (derived from proxy.js responseHeaders and securityHeaders, and lib/portal/index.js's X-WC-Answer-Origin). Header names are lowercase, as Node presents them. The upstream set is closed: anything not listed is dropped, which is the portal's allowlist rule. The upstream x-wc-* headers have two owners: contract 03 (x-wc-relay, x-wc-actor; schemas/03-actor-header.json) and contract 04 (x-wc-level, x-wc-grants, x-wc-decision; schemas/04-level-header.json); x-wc-remote is web-chat's own. This contract adds nothing upstream: its x-wc-embedded and x-wc-embed-parent are response headers on the relayed health (C-06.33), in the downstream set beside 04's x-wc-answer-origin. This file lists each whole set once so a request valid under 04-level-header.json is valid here.

upstream_request.description: Headers on the request the connector makes to 127.0.0.1:<port>. The x-wc-* headers are set AFTER the allowlist, so a viewer can neither send nor suppress them.

^sec-fetch-[a-z-]+$.description: Fetch metadata, forwarded as the portal forwards it (the daemon's browser test reads it).

user-agent.description: Forwarded; the daemon reads it only for push provenance.

origin.description: Present only when the hub matched the viewer's Origin to the surface (or answer) origin; rewritten to the daemon's own loopback origin, as proxy.js does (answer mode: http://127.0.0.1:<answer port>).

x-wc-answer.description: The answer frame's nonce, forwarded in answer mode only (proxy.js ANSWER_HEADER).

x-wc-relay.description: Contract 03's relay secret (C-03.19, C-03.22), 64 lowercase hex, the value handed to this daemon on fd 3 at spawn (C-06.19). Absent only while the connector holds no secret for the running daemon: it restarted while the daemon ran, or it adopted a daemon it did not spawn.

x-wc-actor.description: Contract 03's actor header (C-03.20): one line of compact ASCII JSON validating against schemas/03-actor-header.json, copied verbatim from the relay frame. Absent whenever x-wc-relay is.

x-wc-level.description: Contract 04's daemon level (C-04.9, schemas/04-level-header.json): the decision's daemon_level.

x-wc-grants.description: Contract 04's held levels and true specifics (C-04.9). Absent for a basic decision.

downstream_response.description: Headers the connector adds or replaces on the relayed response (the rest of the daemon's headers pass through minus hop-by-hop and Set-Cookie, as responseHeaders strips them). x-frame-options is not in this set: on every framed document in embedded mode it MUST be absent, because X-Frame-Options cannot name an allowed ancestor.

content-security-policy.description: The frame-ancestors policy the connector appends (one string, or the daemon's policies plus this one). Session documents: frame-ancestors <shell>. Preview paths (/preview/node/*, /preview/pane/*, /replay): frame-ancestors 'self' <shell>. Answer host: frame-ancestors <surface> <shell>. CSP frame-ancestors is checked against every ancestor, so the shell origin must appear in each. <shell> and <surface> are the assignment's origins.shell and origins.surface verbatim, port included: a source without a port matches only https's default port 443 (C-06.31, A-06.2).

x-wc-answer-origin.description: Owned by contract 04 (C-04.9, schemas/04-level-header.json response.x-wc-answer-origin); repeated here so the downstream set is complete. On GET or HEAD /api/health at the surface origin, only when the decision's origins.answer is not null. Carries the hub's port exactly when the hub's public origin does (C-06.29a, A-06.2); 04's own copy is widened by A-04.1 (amendments/04-1).

x-wc-embedded.description: This contract's (C-06.33). On a relayed GET or HEAD /api/health at the surface origin only, added after the daemon's headers and replacing any of the same name, the way x-wc-answer-origin is added. The chrome reads it with headerOf (public/app/remote.js) and applies the embedded layout only when it is also framed. A label: it widens nothing.

x-wc-embed-parent.description: This contract's (C-06.33). The shell origin from the chat assignment's origins.shell, never derived, port included (C-06.29a, A-06.2); on the same responses as x-wc-embedded. The chrome accepts bridge messages only from this origin and posts only to it (C-06.36).

cache-control.description: On /api/* and the framed preview documents, as securityHeaders sets it.
